title: The C.I.A. Helped Pinpoint a Gathering of Iranian Leaders. Then Israel Struck.
partialText: The killing of Iran’s supreme leader and other top Iranian officials came after close intelligence sharing between the United States and Israel, according to people familiar with the operation.

title: Trump, the Self-Declared Peace President, Goes to War Seeking Regime Change
partialText: President Trump has become increasingly willing to assert American power overseas, a decade after propelling himself to the highest office by promising to focus on “America first.”

title: See a Breakdown of Ayatollah Khamenei and Other Top Iranian Leaders
partialText: Among those killed in strikes, according to the U.S. and Israel, were Iran’s supreme leader and three of his top military commanders.

title: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Hard-Line Cleric Who Made Iran a Regional Power, Is Dead at 86
partialText: As Iran’s second supreme leader, he brutally crushed dissent at home and expanded Iran’s footprint abroad, challenging Saudi Arabia for regional dominance.

title: Why the Epstein Investigations Took So Long and Did So Little
partialText: Decades of tips and investigations yielded charges against only two people. A combination of missed chances, narrow laws and prosecutors’ limited focus helps explain why.

title: The U.S. Released the Epstein Files. The Arrests Are Overseas.
partialText: While the latest tranche of documents about the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein has exposed a deeply American scandal, it is Europe where the aggressive enforcement is taking place.

title: How The Times Is Digging Into Millions of Pages of Epstein Files
partialText: Two dozen journalists. A pile of pages that would reach the top of the Empire State Building. And an effort to find the next revelation in a sprawling case.

title: The Texas Senate Primary Offers a Test Case for Each Party
partialText: Should Democrats concentrate on swing voters or their base? Can more traditional Republicans win in the MAGA era? Tuesday’s Senate primary in Texas will show the direction the parties are taking.

title: How Wesley Hunt of Texas Is Working in Plain Sight With Outside Groups
partialText: Exchanges between two X accounts appear to offer a vivid example of how campaigns may sidestep campaign-finance law to share strategic information.

title: In Ukraine, a Community of ‘Simple Believers’ Shuns the Modern World
partialText: The Christians known as viruiuchi prostaky see electricity, cars, higher education and much else as distractions from what really matters.

title: How the Psychedelic Drug Ibogaine Changed Me Forever
partialText: Veterans and others who have suffered trauma and injuries are flocking to clinics around the world to take ibogaine. My own reason was deeply personal.

title: A Tyrant Falls. Dangerous Uncertainty Begins.

title: War and Peace Cannot Be Left to One Man — Especially Not This Man

title: Ask The Morning: Attacks on Iran

title: 3 Killed in Shooting at Bar in Austin

title: ‘One Battle After Another’ Wins Producers Guild Award. Is Oscar Next?

title: Can Nations Agree How to Mine the Sea? This Is the Year, She Says.
partialText: Leticia Carvalho heads a global authority that’s been struggling to set rules for a decade. President Trump’s aggressive push on ocean mining makes her task more urgent.

title: Joe Randall, Chef Who Celebrated Black Cooking Traditions, Dies at 79
partialText: He helped bring the African American cooking of the Carolina Lowcountry to the world and became known as the “dean of Southern Cuisine.”
